guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Three Adult Functions.
The Guide does not need certainty. It chooses the next sane, value-consistent action while the future remains unknown.

(Queue item, not guide prose; what the public guide is asked to preserve:)
### PGQ-014 — Some real problems are blocked, not actionable yet
Preserve the reader-facing distinction between a concrete problem that has a feasible next action and one whose currently relevant steps are all blocked by a known external prerequisite, permission, timing condition, or unavailable resource. In the blocked state, preserve the actual constraint chain and the condition that would reopen action rather than inventing a workaround that assumes a known constraint away. Waiting for a real external condition is not failed motivation or avoidance; put available effort into another useful priority until the route reopens.

### PGQ-017 — One blocked problem should not block the whole life
Preserve the reader-facing distinction between separate practical lanes. When several real problems coexist, one can be externally blocked while another still has a useful next step. Choose the current practical focus from the person's stated goal, impact, urgency, leverage, and what can actually move now; keep the blocked lane's reopening condition visible without letting it suppress an independent actionable priority. When overwhelm makes everything feel scrambled, reduce the sorting burden: one short organizing statement, one prioritized next step, and only a clarification whose answer would genuinely change that next step. Do not make the person define ordinary words or listen to a long recap when the practical implication is already clear enough.

A Healthy Mind Is Not a Perfect Mind. Another form of forced adulthood is demanding a perfectly clean mind. Mental health does not mean never having an ugly, contradictory, shameful, unwanted, or unskillful thought or sensation. A thought can appear without your endorsing it. The Guide’s job is not to police every mental event. It is to notice what appeared, distinguish it from intention and identity, choose what is skillful and consistent with your values, and let the rest pass without turning it into a permanent verdict.

I think this is closer to Buddhist practice too. The point is not an impossible performance in which nothing unskillful ever appears. In AN 6.63, the Buddha defines kamma in terms of intention; MN 20 gives practitioners several ways to work with unskillful thoughts when they arise; and DN 2 treats recognizing a fault, making amends, and restraining oneself going forward as growth in the training. That is a model of discernment, training, and repair—not mental purity as identity. Shame about a chosen action can sometimes signal that something needs attention; shame about an intrusive thought merely for appearing is not the same thing. The useful move is “learn, repair, choose more skillfully,” not “this proves what I am forever.”
brief:
- the meaning, in plain words: the Guide doesn't need to know how things will turn out; it picks the next sensible step that fits what you care about while the future stays unknown. Some problems have a next step you can take; in others everything that matters is blocked from outside (a prerequisite, a permission, timing, a missing resource). For a blocked one: keep in view what you're waiting on and what would reopen it; don't invent a workaround that assumes the block away; waiting on a real outside condition isn't laziness or avoidance; meanwhile put your effort into something else useful that can move, and don't let the blocked one crowd it out. When several problems coexist, one can be blocked while another still has a next step; choose the current focus by what you're going for, what matters most, what can't wait and what can move now. When overwhelm scrambles everything: one short sentence that sorts it, one next step, and only a question whose answer would change that step.
- context, not for the text: the guide's own "Don't make the person define ordinary words or listen to a long recap" is how a helper talks to someone, so it stays in the AI guide (E156); the article speaks to the person doing the work.
- context, not for the text: the dedup for this group is experiments/t56-guide/DEDUP-REPORT.md, Group 4; When to Change the Strategy's "I'd work on that one thing instead of giving up on everything" is about an obstacle you can work on, not one blocked from outside.
- group 5, the meaning in plain words: demanding a perfectly clean mind is forced adulthood too. Mental health doesn't mean never having an ugly, contradictory, shameful or unwanted thought, or a sensation you didn't ask for; a thought can show up without your agreeing with it. The Guide doesn't police every thought: it notices what showed up, tells it apart from what you mean to do and from who you are, goes with what fits what you care about, and lets the rest pass without making it a verdict on you. Transient thoughts can still be signals (Catch the Hook Before the Story Takes Over), so don't make it throwing everything away.
- group 6, the meaning in plain words: this is closer to Buddhist practice too. The practice isn't a performance where nothing unskillful ever shows up: in AN 6.63 the Buddha says kamma is intention; MN 20 gives several ways to work with unskillful thoughts once they arise; in DN 2 recognizing a fault, making amends and restraint from then on count as growth in the training. That's seeing clearly, practice and repair, not mental purity as who you are. Shame about something you chose to do can sometimes signal that something needs attention; shame about a thought merely for appearing is a different thing.
- context, not for the text: the dedup is experiments/t56-guide/DEDUP-REPORT.md, Groups 5 and 6; the article already has scary thoughts not making you a bad person (Hold the Child Only When You're Ready), ill will hurting the one who has it and loving-kindness for ill will (the Buddha passages), and "What can you learn or repair now". The sutta links in P8 go to SuttaCentral (AN 6.63, MN 20, DN 2).
